Anyone relying on table extraction for SQL expressions (query validation, variable interpolation) gets a guaranteed error; the surrounding JSON parsing logic at lines 25+ can never execute and will silently rot.

records.issue_text: [BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false on both branches, so the featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions flag can never enable SQL expressions and every QueryTypeSQL request fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. Any user submitting a SQL expression query gets an error even with the feature flag enabled; the flag is a dead toggle and the gate logic `if enabled { return false }` is inverted/nonsensical (it returns false in both the enabled and disabled cases).
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the new QueryTypeSQL branch calls enableSqlExpressions(h) and returns an error when it’s false: `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`. The newly added `enableSqlExpressions` function always returns false regardless of flag state (`if enabled { return false }` then `return false`), so every SQL expression query will always hit the error path.

records.issue_text: [BUG] NewInMemoryDB returns a stub whose RunCommands and QueryFramesInto unconditionally return errors.New("not implemented"), silently replacing the working go-duck implementation that was deleted. Every SQL expression execute path (SQLCommand.Execute via sql_command.go:96-100) and every TablesList call (parser.go:23-25) now fails at runtime with 'not implemented' for all users — a hard functional regression on the request path reported only as a query error, not surfaced as an API-shape or build-time signal.
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/parser.go, TablesList now calls duckDB := NewInMemoryDB() and then ret, err := duckDB.RunCommands(...). The newly added pkg/expr/sql/db.go defines (*DB).RunCommands(...) to always return an error ("not implemented"), so TablesList will always error and the subsequent JSON parsing/flattening logic in TablesList can never run. This makes table extraction non-functional as introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The error returned when SQL expressions are disabled is a raw fmt.Errorf surfaced to the expression API rather than an errutil-derived 4xx-style error, and its text describes implementation status rather than the feature being toggled off. Users with the feature flag disabled receive a misleading 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' message that misdirects debugging (suggests a bug rather than a disabled flag), and the error bypasses the errutil envelope used elsewhere in sql_command.go for error classification.
records.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, the SQL query path now gates on enableSqlExpressions(h) and returns a raw fmt.Errorf with the message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" when disabled: `if !enabled { return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented") }`. This directly matches the finding: the error is not errutil-derived and the text describes implementation status rather than the feature flag being off. Additionally, enableSqlExpressions currently returns false in all cases, making this error path unavoidable, further confirming the user-facing impact.
